fns.desc: wpa_auth_eid_key_delivery() takes a max_len parameter (remaining space in the association-response buffer) but never references it anywhere in the body -- it writes the Key Delivery element (header + fragmented KDE data, size driven by GTK/IGTK/BIGTK/ieee80211w KDE lengths) with no bound check against max_len at all. Upstream's own comment at line 7989 flags this: "TODO: Make sure there is sufficient length for the element." Caller wpa_auth_write_assoc_resp_eppke passes end-pos as max_len but that value is silently dropped, so a sufficiently large KDE payload can overflow the caller's association-response buffer.
